* chore(x-charts): stryker mutation testing baseline (advisory)

Faz 21.9 PR3f (Codex thread `019defa5`). Adds the missing mutation-test
infrastructure for `@mfe/x-charts`. The package was wrongly listed as
`mutation-tested` in the chart-detail catalog until PR #188 corrected
the false claim; this PR makes the claim true.

Scope (Codex review: keep it dar)
- Mutate target is the pure-function surface only:
  - src/responsive/buildResponsive*.ts
  - src/responsive/useResponsiveLegend.ts
  - src/responsive/useAutoGranularity.ts
  - src/responsive/useResponsiveChartType.ts
  - src/chartSize.ts
  - src/cross-filter/createCrossFilterStore.ts
  - src/cross-filter/eventBridge.ts
  - src/cross-filter/selectors.ts
  - src/cross-filter/useQueryCancellation.ts
  - src/useResponsiveChart.ts
- Chart wrappers excluded — their tests render ECharts canvases that
  timeout under mutation analysis. Wrappers stay covered via
  option-shape tests + visual regression instead.

Operational
- `pnpm --filter @mfe/x-charts test:mutation` runs locally
- CI is NOT auto-wired in this PR. Codex review: "İlk PR'da
  x-charts-quality-gates.yml hard gate'e ekleme. workflow_dispatch
  veya nightly/advisory başlat." Workflow integration follows in a
  separate PR after the first 2-3 advisory runs surface a real
  baseline.
- `break` threshold intentionally low (10%) so the first mutation
  baseline doesn't fail CI on day 1.

Tooling
- @stryker-mutator/core@^9.6.1 + vitest-runner@^9.6.1 (same versions
  as packages/design-system to keep monorepo consistent)
- .gitignore added for .stryker-cache + reports/mutation

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(deps): add stryker x-charts to pnpm-lock for pr3f

pr.body:
## Summary

Faz 21.9 PR3f. Adds missing mutation-test infrastructure for `@mfe/x-charts`. Package was wrongly listed as `mutation-tested` until PR #188 corrected the false claim; this PR makes the claim true.

## Scope (Codex review: keep it dar)

Mutate target is **pure-function surface only**:
- `src/responsive/buildResponsive*.ts` (4 helpers)
- `src/responsive/useResponsiveLegend.ts`, `useAutoGranularity.ts`, `useResponsiveChartType.ts`
- `src/chartSize.ts` (PR3a contract)
- `src/cross-filter/createCrossFilterStore.ts`, `eventBridge.ts`, `selectors.ts`, `useQueryCancellation.ts`
- `src/useResponsiveChart.ts`

**Chart wrappers excluded** — tests render ECharts canvases that timeout under mutation analysis. Wrappers covered via option-shape + visual regression.

## Operational

- `pnpm --filter @mfe/x-charts test:mutation` runs locally
- **CI not auto-wired**. Codex review explicit: "İlk PR'da hard gate'e ekleme. workflow_dispatch veya nightly/advisory başlat." Workflow integration is a follow-up PR after 2-3 advisory runs surface a real baseline.
- `break: 10%` threshold intentionally low so day-1 baseline doesn't fail CI.

## Tooling

- `@stryker-mutator/core@^9.6.1` + `vitest-runner@^9.6.1` (same versions as `packages/design-system`)
- `.gitignore` for `.stryker-cache` + `reports/mutation`

pr.body:
## Shared TypeScript Base Config

### Summary
This PR adds a shared TypeScript base config for the app and packages/shared.

### Changes
- ✅ tsconfig.base.json with shared compiler options
- ✅ Root tsconfig.json extends base
- ✅ packages/shared/tsconfig.json extends base
- ✅ Verification script
- ✅ README updated

### Benefits
- Single source of truth for TypeScript options
- Consistent compiler settings across targets
- Easier to maintain and update
- Reduces duplication

### Files Added
- tsconfig.base.json
- scripts/verify-tsconfig.sh
- packages/shared/tsconfig.json

### Files Modified
- tsconfig.json
- package.json
- README.md

Closes #872

pr.body:
## Problem

Endings are recognised only from the live transcript. When the recognizer mishears a short ending (#69 records `paste that` heard as `Haste that`), nothing happens: the user can't tell why, and either repeats it or waits for the idle limit.

## Change

A small local keyword spotter (sherpa-onnx's `kws-zipformer-gigaspeech-3.3M`, Apache-2.0, int8, 6.3 MB from the model author's ModelScope repo, SHA-256 pinned in `ModelStore`) listens to the same frames the recognizer gets, for every live speech-server entry. It tokenizes the configured endings when it loads.

- When the live final covering a heard ending lacks it, and the user then stays quiet for that ending's pause, the cancelled cue plays. The overlay then shows `Heard “paste that”, but the transcript did not end with it. Nothing was removed; say the ending again.` until the next words are heard.
- Nothing is cut, retried or acted on because of the spotter. The transcript's endings work as before, and holds give the spotter no frames.
- A late final that does carry the ending (up to 3 s, about twice the longest delay measured) is normal agreement and stays silent. Continued speech dismisses a dispute silently.
- An ending the model can't hear, such as a German phrase, turns the spotter off with one notice naming the phrase; the config still loads.
- `Event::EndingSpotter` records the load, each hit's confidence and verdict, and a per-capture summary. It records no words.
- Every model download now sends a `User-Agent`, because ModelScope's CDN refuses requests without one.

This replaces #91's "cut at the timestamp", as the developer decided. A hit's time is token emission, 0.2–0.5 s after the word starts, and finals carry no word times, so a cut leaked command fragments in 3 of 4 controls. Re-transcribing the disputed audio rescued 0 of 12 disputes on 62.8 min of dictation, so the notice-only variant ships. The new `DECISIONS.md` bullet records why.

## Platforms

- GNOME Wayland: the headless sandboxed rig (`up --gnome`) with synthetic Kokoro speech fed into the sandbox microphone and a fake recognizer.
- Hyprland and Windows: CI and fake-based tests only.

## Verification

- Refreshed against `development` at `b6b96e7`, preserving the speech-server list, agent controls, model-download header and pinned-size limit. The active speech entry and partial/final lag metrics remain covered. Whole-text tasks are not mistaken for spoken endings.
- **All 19 hosted checks passed on `15c2c86`.** All eight mutation reports finished and covered 559 distinct mutants exactly once: 467 caught, 19 surviving, 8 timed out and 65 unviable. Reports and archive checksums were reviewed. Neither of the previous runner shutdowns recurred.
- The previous report review found 12 further missing assertions. The test-only follow-up `15c2c86` adds overlapping/suffix phrase matches and scores, stable addition of beam probabilities, unknown/truncated fixed64 protobuf fields, and invalid encoder chunk lengths. The complete hosted sweep now catches all 12 mutations addressed by that follow-up. Runtime spotter code and all mapped cancellation hashes are unchanged.
- Latest Linux `gates server`: UI build, formatting, lint, **680 Rust tests passed** (6 existing tests ignored), docs with warnings denied, and AppImage packaging. The complete workspace also passes under the mutation job's 4 GiB virtual-memory bound. Earlier desktop UI gate (181 tests), cargo-deny and workflow lint passed; staged and outgoing secret scans found no leaks. No mutation exclusions or test expectations were weakened.
- Real current app in an isolated GNOME Wayland sandbox, real keyword model, synthetic WAV input and a fake realtime recognizer: all 12 acceptance assertions pass. A missed ending warns without delivery; repetition copies every original dictated word once; matching endings stay silent; cancellation copies nothing. Active-entry and lag metrics, agent settings/metrics readback, and pause/resume also pass. Screenshot evidence stays outside Git. The private rig uses a microphone-feeder pacing correction; the repository helper is unchanged. The latest follow-up only changes tests, so this runtime result still applies.
- Cancellation verification passes with current source hashes: full bounded model (7,481 states), both negative controls and the real-code cancellation/hold/settings replay. The source map names inspected code commit `68d7e14`. The metric-summary extraction preserves all mapped functions and await boundaries.
- Of the full hosted run's 19 survivors, 15 are equivalent within the stated input contracts: finite changes to the zero-weight first window sample; inactive sample clamps; an empty drain; zero filter-edge weights; extra FFT bins outside every filter; exchanging equal log probabilities; and an overwritten path score. For the checksum-pinned model only, the encoder always declares 80 bins, its 45-frame window already fails the whole-step condition at equality, and both preflight contexts are legal with discarded outputs. These judgments do not cover other models. Four remaining survivors alter only the test fake's synthetic hit timestamps; those are fixture coverage limitations, not claimed equivalent as a fake API.
- The advisory retains eight independent baseline-tested shards and separate artifacts. Two deliberately unbounded allocation controls fail with allocator errors under the 4 GiB limit; normal workspace tests pass under the same limit. CI disables core dumps. Earlier interrupted logs establish runner shutdown signals, not their underlying cause.

candidates.message:
docs(claude): a release runs five things locally, and they are now a rule

Asked why the screenshots were not refreshed for 0.11.0, the honest answer is
that it was not written where the rules are. Rule 11 lists five files to edit
and says nothing about running anything; the screenshot step existed only as
guidance in docs/development.md. So rule 26 now says what a release *runs*
before the bump, in order, with the reason each one earned its place.

Writing the rule was not enough on its own, which is the part worth recording.
The capture script was broken too, by the same closed-by-default flip that
broke conformance and soak: its demo service declares a hostname and no gate,
so the traffic it drives to make the screens worth looking at never arrived,
and it failed with "the demo traffic did not reach the server being captured".
That is a fourth harness with one cause. Fixed the same way, and the fresh
capture is in this commit, twelve images including the clients table that now
has a name column.

Two suites move off CI, as asked, and both had a reason beyond being slow.

Mutation testing is hours across eight runners and is now workflow_dispatch
only. The workflow stays because a runner is still the right place for the
whole set when somebody wants it.

Autobahn is out of the conformance workflow entirely. Its pinned image tag,
0.8.2, is not published: the image moved to date-based tags, so the pull
failed with "manifest unknown", which is a CI failure about somebody else's
registry rather than about this project. The tag is corrected to one that
exists, 25.10.1, so the local run works. h2spec stays in CI, since it
downloads a binary and needs nothing.

Both are in rule 26's list, which is where a thing that no longer runs
automatically has to be if it is going to run at all.

changes.message:
test(mutation): add non-blocking mutation-testing scaffold

StrykerJS (make mutate-js, incremental, scoped to clean_adblock/
picker.js) and mutmut (make mutate-py, the three test-py source
packages, test files excluded). Neither is wired into make precommit;
a weekly continue-on-error workflow runs both informationally.

Smoke results: stryker 146 mutants / score 41.78% in 9s; mutmut 1012
mutants, 292 killed / 575 survived / 143 no-tests. Documented the
mutmut 3.6.0 incompatibility with tests that patch os.getcwd (8
retriever tests excluded via -k) and the do_not_mutate fix that keeps
test files from being mutated.

Upgrade tools (#7)

* Upgrade PHPStan to 2.x
* Upgrade Psalm
* require PHP 8.3
* upgrade Infection
* upgrade PHPUnit
* upgrade GitHub workflow actions
* normalize composer.json
* remove running CI with prefer-lowest deps. It doesn't make sense in a package without dependencies
* use dataProvider attributes

---------

Co-authored-by: Thomas Rieschl <thomas@trinet.at>

candidates.message:
ci: call the Mutants and Fuzz workflows of oxirush-aper that every crate shares

The jobs of the Mutants and Fuzz workflows are those of
crate-mutants.yml and crate-fuzz.yml of oxirush-aper at 7ff6f4d, which
every crate of the family calls with its own numbers: its shards, its
targets, its schedule and the targets that run at once. The jobs of the
crate's own stay here. .github/mutants-recheck.py goes: the shared
workflow has the script.

The fuzzing of a run ends within eight hours: a target runs less than
its minutes when the targets, in rounds of as many as run at once, would
take longer.

Signed-off-by: valentin <valentin@devling.xyz>

candidates.message:
Add make metrics, and record the throughput baseline (#97)

Reports PR lead time, the split around the first review, CI reruns and
issues completed per week from GitHub's data. The ADR gets the baseline
for the PRs merged between the ruleset and the S1-S7 changes, and when to
measure again.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

pr.body:
## Summary

Carries out the first two criteria of M6 from ADR-0001. See #86, which stays open for the re-measure from 2026-11-20.

- `make metrics` runs `scripts/metrics.py`, which reads from GitHub through `gh` and uses only the Python standard library. It takes `--since`, `--until` and `--prs` through `ARGS`.
- It reports PR lead time, the time before and after the first review, CI reruns per PR, and issues completed per week.
- The ADR gets a Baseline section. Its status and decisions don't change.

## Baseline

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Median PR lead time | 44.5 min, 8 PRs |
| Median open to first review | 24.5 min, 6 PRs |
| Median first review to merge | 20 min, 6 PRs |
| Mean CI reruns per PR | 0.88, 8 PRs |

The window is the PRs merged after the ruleset in #50 and before #88. Earlier PRs had no CI gates, so they'd make the baseline look faster than it was.

The split around the first review doesn't show which side is the bigger lever, and it moves with the window. So this doesn't settle #77.

## Design notes

- The script stays out of CI, because its output changes with live data and it needs a network.
- Agents and the owner share an account, so any review that isn't from a bot counts. The ADR lists this and the other limits.
- Local hook times aren't on GitHub, so they aren't measured.
- There's no automated test for the script, because CI has no Python step and I didn't want to add one for this.

## Testing

- `make ci` passes. No file in `src/` or `tests/` changed, so the demo output can't differ from `main`.
- `make metrics` reproduces the ADR's numbers.
- The output was compared by hand with #62 and #88: 52 and 27 minutes of lead time, and 2 reruns each.
- A bad date gives an argument error, and a missing `gh` stops `make metrics` with a non-zero exit code.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

changes.message: Add advisory incremental mutation testing on PRs (#131)

pr.body:
## Summary

- Run diff-scoped mutation testing on PR merge commits through `make mutants-diff`, without adding a required check or changing the weekly full run.
- Report elapsed time and results in Actions and post a separate comment for same-repository PRs; fork PR results remain in Actions.
- Document coverage limitations and test reporting and error handling.

Closes #82.

## Validation

- `make ci`
- `make mutants-test`
- `actionlint .github/workflows/mutants-pr.yml`
- Real diff-scoped mutation run and fixture runs covering surviving mutants, baseline failure, and a diff without Rust changes.

Live GitHub Actions and fork permissions have not yet been verified.
